claims.claim: The expression of NE factors was eliminated in SCLC by inhibition of HDACs using trichostatin A, even in the absence of KRASG12V induction.
claims.source: Inversely, the expression of NE factors was eliminated in SCLC by inhibition of histone deacetylases (HDACs) using trichostatin A, even in the absence of KRASG12V induction, suggesting that H3K27ac levels must be restricted to maintain SCLC lineage (Figure 4d).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: H3K27ac levels must be restricted to maintain SCLC lineage.
claims.source: Inversely, the expression of NE factors was eliminated in SCLC by inhibition of histone deacetylases (HDACs) using trichostatin A, even in the absence of KRASG12V induction, suggesting that H3K27ac levels must be restricted to maintain SCLC lineage (Figure 4d).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the HDAC inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: Constitutively activated ERK suppresses NETFs partly through MSK but mostly via reconfiguration of chromatin structure by CBP/p300 in a subset of SCLC.
claims.source: Although A-485 treatment did not rescue the ERK-mediated suppression of NE factors in H2107 and H524 cells even when combined with MSK inhibition (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a) or with HES1 knockout (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c), these results collectively suggest that constitutively activated ERK suppresses NETFs partly through MSK but mostly via reconfiguration of chromatin structure by CBP/p300 in a subset of SCLC.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the combined inhibitor experiments and cell line-specific responses.

claims.claim: Induction of KRASG12V expression with doxycycline caused an overall increase in chromatin accessibility.
claims.source: Overall, induction of KRASG12V expression with doxycycline caused an overall increase in chromatin accessibility (H82: 88 peaks of chromatin accessibility gained; 36 lost; H2107: 38 gained, one lost; H524 638 gained,703 lost).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ATAC-seq data.

claims.claim: Addition of the ERK inhibitor SCH772984 led to a reduction in the number of peaks of accessible chromatin.
claims.source: On the contrary, addition of the ERK inhibitor SCH772984 led to a reduction in the number of peaks of accessible chromatin (H82: 131 lost, 58 gained; H2107: 36 lost, one gained; H524: 503 lost, 345 gained; Figure 5a and b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5a and b.

claims.claim: The locales of altered accessibility were primarily located in intergenic and intronic regions, in keeping with shifts primarily occurring in regulatory regions, including putative enhancers.
claims.source: The locales of altered accessibility were primarily located in intergenic and intronic regions, in keeping with shifts primarily occurring in regulatory regions, including putative enhancers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1c and d).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1c and d.

claims.claim: Doxycycline treatment led to increased accessibility around ETV1 and ETV4 DNA binding motifs, as well as motifs associated with AP-1 family members.
claims.source: Motif analysis showed that doxycycline treatment led to increased accessibility around ETV1 and ETV4 DNA binding motifs, as well as motifs associated with AP-1 family members, and reduced accessibility at NEUROD1 and ASCL1 motifs (Figure 5c).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by motif analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5c.

claims.claim: Doxycycline treatment reduced accessibility at NEUROD1 and ASCL1 motifs.
claims.source: Motif analysis showed that doxycycline treatment led to increased accessibility around ETV1 and ETV4 DNA binding motifs, as well as motifs associated with AP-1 family members, and reduced accessibility at NEUROD1 and ASCL1 motifs (Figure 5c).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by motif analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5c.

claims.claim: Treatment with SCH772984 reversed the pattern of chromatin accessibility changes induced by doxycycline.
claims.source: A reversal of this pattern was observed upon treatment with SCH772984 (Figure 5d).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by motif analysis of ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 5d.

claims.claim: Peaks gained upon doxycycline induction were associated with areas of chromatin decorated with H3K27ac.
claims.source: Permutation testing showed that peaks gained upon doxycycline induction, with or without SCH779284, were associated with areas of chromatin decorated with H3K27ac (p=0.002, hypergeometric test; Figure 5e and f), a histone post-translational modification associated with open chromatin, in control normal human lung.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by permutation testing shown in Figure 5e and f.

claims.claim: Doxycycline induction led to markedly increased accessibility at the ETV1 and ETV4 binding motifs in H524 and H82 cells.
claims.source: Motif accessibility profiles within differentially accessible regions showed that doxycycline induction led to markedly increased accessibility at the ETV1 and ETV4 binding motifs in H524 and H82 cells (Figure 5g).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by motif occupancy profiles shown in Figure 5g.

claims.claim: Chromatin accessibility was reduced at putative binding motifs for ASCL1 and NEUROD1 in H524 and H2107 after doxycycline induction.
claims.source: In contrast, chromatin accessibility was reduced at putative binding motifs for neuroendocrine lineage TFs, including ASCL1 and NEUROD1 in H524 and H2107 (Figure 5h).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by motif occupancy profiles shown in Figure 5h.

claims.claim: ATAC-seq demonstrated global chromatin rewiring at ETS transcriptional targets upon KRASG12V induction in SCLC cells.
claims.source: ATAC-seq demonstrated global chromatin rewiring at ETS transcriptional targets upon KRASG12V induction in SCLC cells.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ATAC-seq data showing changes in accessibility at ETS motifs.

claims.claim: ETS TFs – including ETV1, ETV4, and ETV5 – were upregulated at the mRNA level by activation of MAPK.
claims.source: Furthermore, ETS TFs – including the PEA3 family of ETS TFs, ETV1, ETV4, and ETV5 – were upregulated at the mRNA level by activation of MAPK (Supplementary file 1 and Figure 6a), suggesting that an ETS TFs-mediated program may play a role in suppressing NE differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by microarray data shown in Supplementary file 1 and Figure 6a.

claims.claim: An ETS TFs-mediated program may play a role in suppressing NE differentiation.
claims.source: Furthermore, ETS TFs – including the PEA3 family of ETS TFs, ETV1, ETV4, and ETV5 – were upregulated at the mRNA level by activation of MAPK (Supplementary file 1 and Figure 6a), suggesting that an ETS TFs-mediated program may play a role in suppressing NE differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the upregulation of ETS TFs and chromatin accessibility changes.

claims.claim: Microarray data of SCLC and LUAD cell lines indicated a clear inverse relationship of expression of PEA3 family ETS TFs with that of NETFs.
claims.source: Indeed, microarray data of SCLC and LUAD cell lines indicated the clear inverse relationship of expression of PEA3 family ETS TFs with that of NETFs (Figure 6b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by microarray data shown in Figure 6b.

claims.claim: Mutant KRAS upregulates ETV4 in H82 and H524 cells and ETV5 in all three SCLC lines.
claims.source: At the protein level, we found that mutant KRAS upregulates ETV4 in H82 and H524 cells and ETV5 in all the three SCLC lines, which was completely reversed by ERK inhibition with SCH772984 (Figure 6c).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: ERK inhibition with SCH772984 completely reversed the upregulation of ETV4 and ETV5 by mutant KRAS.
claims.source: At the protein level, we found that mutant KRAS upregulates ETV4 in H82 and H524 cells and ETV5 in all the three SCLC lines, which was completely reversed by ERK inhibition with SCH772984 (Figure 6c).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6c.

claims.claim: Conditional expression of ETV1 in SCLC cells led to suppression of specific NETFs.
claims.source: To test this, we conditionally expressed ETV1 in the three SCLC cell lines, which led to suppression of specific NETFs – notably ASCL1 in H2107, INSM1 and NEUROD1 in H82, and BRN2 in H524 (Figure 6d).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6d.

claims.claim: Conditional expression of ETV5 significantly downregulated INSM1 and NEUROD1 in H82, and NEUROD1 in H524.
claims.source: Conditional expression of ETV5 also significantly downregulated INSM1 and NEUROD1 in H82, and NEUROD1 in H524 (Figure 6e).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6e.

claims.claim: ETV1- or ETV5-overexpressing cells transformed to an adherent phenotype.
claims.source: Furthermore, ETV1- or ETV5-overexpressing cells unexpectedly transformed to an adherent phenotype, with this morphological change most strongly observed in H82 cells, similar to what is observed with KRASG12V induction (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by microscopy images shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: ETV4 knockdown modestly restored suppressed INSM1 while ETV5 knockdown restored NEUROD1.
claims.source: Next, we conducted knockdown of ETV4, ETV5, or both using siRNAs in mutant KRAS-inducible H82 cells and found that ETV4 knockdown modestly restored suppressed INSM1 while ETV5 knockdown restored NEUROD1 (Figure 6f).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6f.

claims.claim: Dual knockdown of ETV4 and ETV5 jointly increased INSM1 and CD56 expression.
claims.source: Importantly, dual knockdown of ETV4 and ETV5 jointly increased INSM1 and CD56 expression, suggesting the functional redundancy of different ETS factors, such that knockdown of a single or two factors is unable to completely mitigate the effects of ERK activation.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6f.

claims.claim: There is functional redundancy of different ETS factors in suppressing NE differentiation.
claims.source: Importantly, dual knockdown of ETV4 and ETV5 jointly increased INSM1 and CD56 expression, suggesting the functional redundancy of different ETS factors, such that knockdown of a single or two factors is unable to completely mitigate the effects of ERK activation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the dual knockdown experiments showing additive effects.

claims.claim: Nuclear CIC was expressed in SCLC cells and downregulated after KRASG12V induction, which was restored by ERK inhibition.
claims.source: We confirmed that nuclear CIC was expressed in SCLC cells and downregulated after KRASG12V induction, which was restored by ERK inhibition (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot of fractionated lysates shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2a.

claims.claim: siRNA knockdown of CIC led to downregulation of INSM1, NEUROD1, and to a lesser extent BRN2 in H82 cells.
claims.source: siRNA knockdown of CIC led to downregulation of INSM1, NEUROD1, and to a lesser extent BRN2 in H82 cells and potentiated the effects of mutant KRAS induction on NE factor suppression in H82 and H524 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2b.

claims.claim: CIC knockdown was not sufficient to induce ETV1, ETV4, and ETV5.
claims.source: However, CIC knockdown was not sufficient to induce ETV1, ETV4, and ETV5.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2b.

claims.claim: Overexpression of CIC did not inhibit suppression of NE factors after KRASG12V induction.
claims.source: Likewise, overexpression of CIC did not inhibit suppression of NE factors after KRASG12V induction (Figure 6—figure supplement 2c), as exogenous CIC was putatively inactivated following immediate phosphorylation by activated ERK.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2c.

claims.claim: ERK-mediated upregulation of the PEA3 family of ETS TFs does not occur via CIC inhibition in SCLC cells.
claims.source: These results suggest that ERK-mediated upregulation of the PEA3 family of ETS TFs does not occur via CIC inhibition in SCLC cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the CIC knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claims.claim: A-485 treatment downregulates ERK-induced ETV4 and ETV5 in H82-KRAS cells but not in H2107- and H524-KRAS cells.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that A-485 treatment downregulates ERK-induced ETV4 and ETV5 in H82-KRAS cells but not in H2107- and H524-KRAS cells, providing a potential biological explanation why CBP/p300 inhibition rescues ERK-mediated suppression of NE differentiation only in H82 cells (Figure 6g and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6g and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claims.claim: ERG was not basally expressed in the three SCLC cell lines but was induced by KRASG12V in H82 and H524 cells.
claims.source: ERG was not basally expressed in the three SCLC cell lines but was induced by KRASG12V in H82 and H524 cells.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3a.

claims.claim: Inhibition of ERG in H82 cells after KRASG12V activation provided modest restoration of INSM1, BRN2, and NEUROD1 at the optimal concentration of 0.6 μM, which synergized with MSK/RSK co-inhibition.
claims.source: Inhibition of ERG in H82 cells after KRASG12V activation provided modest restoration of INSM1, BRN2, and NEUROD1 at the optimal concentration of 0.6 μM, which synergized with MSK/RSK co-inhibition.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3a.

claims.claim: Suppression of MYC by KRASG12V was well rescued by combined MSK/RSK and ERG inhibition that did not rescue suppressed expression of key NETFs.
claims.source: Interestingly, treatment of H82-KRASG12V cells with different combinations of inhibitors targeting MSK/RSK, CBP/p300, or ERG revealed that suppression of MYC by KRASG12V was well rescued by combined MSK/RSK and ERG inhibition that did not rescue suppressed expression of key NETFs, suggesting that oncogene-mediated ERK activation in SCLC modulates essential TFs through multiple regulatory mechanisms (Figure 6—figure supplement 3b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3b.

claims.claim: Oncogene-mediated ERK activation in SCLC modulates essential TFs through multiple regulatory mechanisms.
claims.source: Interestingly, treatment of H82-KRASG12V cells with different combinations of inhibitors targeting MSK/RSK, CBP/p300, or ERG revealed that suppression of MYC by KRASG12V was well rescued by combined MSK/RSK and ERG inhibition that did not rescue suppressed expression of key NETFs, suggesting that oncogene-mediated ERK activation in SCLC modulates essential TFs through multiple regulatory mechanisms (Figure 6—figure supplement 3b).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the differential rescue effects of various inhibitor combinations.

claims.claim: ERK-induced ETS factor expression suppresses NE lineage factors in SCLC.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that ERK-induced ETS factor expression suppresses NE lineage factors in SCLC and that induction of the PEA3 family of ETS TFs is mediated by the HAT activity of CBP/p300 in H82 cells but not in H2107 and H524 cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the ETS overexpression and knockdown experiments.

claims.claim: Induction of the PEA3 family of ETS TFs is mediated by the HAT activity of CBP/p300 in H82 cells but not in H2107 and H524 cells.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that ERK-induced ETS factor expression suppresses NE lineage factors in SCLC and that induction of the PEA3 family of ETS TFs is mediated by the HAT activity of CBP/p300 in H82 cells but not in H2107 and H524 cells.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the differential effects of CBP/p300 inhibition in different cell lines.

claims.claim: Dual p53/RB inactivation is ubiquitous in SCLC.
claims.source: Dual p53/RB inactivation is ubiquitous in SCLC (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015), and EGFR-mutant LUADs with p53/RB loss are more likely to undergo SCLC transformation after TKI treatment (Offin et al., 2019; Niederst et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Peifer et al., 2012 and George et al., 2015.

claims.claim: EGFR-mutant LUADs with p53/RB loss are more likely to undergo SCLC transformation after TKI treatment.
claims.source: Dual p53/RB inactivation is ubiquitous in SCLC (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015), and EGFR-mutant LUADs with p53/RB loss are more likely to undergo SCLC transformation after TKI treatment (Offin et al., 2019; Niederst et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Offin et al., 2019; Niederst et al., 2015; and Lee et al., 2017.

claims.claim: Deregulation of SOX2 was not observed following osimertinib treatment in RB1-knockout PC9 and H1975 cells, irrespective of the RB1 status.
claims.source: Unlike the prostate cancer scenario, deregulation of SOX2 was not observed following osimertinib treatment, irrespective of the RB1 status (Figure 6—figure supplement 4b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4b.

claims.claim: NE factors were not induced in the triple-mutant (TP53/RB1/EGFR) clones after osimertinib treatment.
claims.source: In addition, NE factors were not induced in the triple-mutant clones, suggesting that the LUAD lineage is more strictly maintained than the lineage of AR-dependent prostate cancer in the context of dual p53/RB inactivation, confirming a previous study (Niederst et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4b.

claims.claim: The LUAD lineage is more strictly maintained than the lineage of AR-dependent prostate cancer in the context of dual p53/RB inactivation.
claims.source: In addition, NE factors were not induced in the triple-mutant clones, suggesting that the LUAD lineage is more strictly maintained than the lineage of AR-dependent prostate cancer in the context of dual p53/RB inactivation, confirming a previous study (Niederst et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the lack of NE factor induction and is consistent with a previous study.

claims.claim: pERK was still detectable in the majority of osimertinib-resistant clones in the presence of osimertinib.
claims.source: Correspondingly, pERK was still detectable in the majority of resistant clones in the presence of osimertinib (Figure 6—figure supplement 4f), unlike parental cell lines with acute treatment (Figure 6—figure supplement 4b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4f.

claims.claim: No induced expression of the main NE factors was observed in osimertinib-resistant cells.
claims.source: Western blot analysis also confirmed no induced expression of the main NE factors in resistant cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 4f).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4f.

claims.claim: CIC mutations were recurrently identified in H1975 osimertinib-resistant clones.
claims.source: Importantly, CIC mutations that bypass the requirement for upstream MAPK pathway reactivation were recurrently identified in H1975 resistant clones (Figure 6—figure supplement 4e), which was validated by western blot (Figure 6—figure supplement 4g).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by MSK-IMPACT sequencing and western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4e and g.

claims.claim: ETV5 was most prominently upregulated in osimertinib-resistant clones harboring acquired CIC alterations.
claims.source: Among the PEA3 family of ETS TFs, ETV5 was most prominently upregulated in osimertinib-resistant clones harboring acquired CIC alterations (Figure 6—figure supplement 4g).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4g.

claims.claim: Recurrently observed resistance mechanisms that reactivate the ERK/CIC/ETS axis might suppress the NE differentiation program during chronic inhibition of drivers even in the context of p53/RB loss.
claims.source: These data collectively suggest that recurrently observed resistance mechanisms that reactivate the ERK/CIC/ETS axis might suppress the NE differentiation program during chronic inhibition of drivers even in the context of p53/RB loss.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of MAPK reactivation and CIC mutations in resistant cells without NE transformation.

claims.claim: Inhibition of ERK and MSK/RSK in stem cell culture media induced a neuronal-like appearance in H1975 cells.
claims.source: Interestingly, inhibition of ERK and MSK/RSK in SCCM inhibited the phenotypic change into floating suspension. Furthermore, cells developed a neuronal-like appearance showing bipolar or multipolar cells with axonal processes after combined inhibition of ERK and MSK/RSK regardless of RB1 status (Figure 6—figure supplement 5a), which was coupled with suppression of EGFR (Figure 6—figure supplement 5b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by microscopy images shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5a.

claims.claim: Combined inhibition of ERK and MSK/RSK was coupled with suppression of EGFR in H1975 cells cultured in SCCM.
claims.source: Interestingly, inhibition of ERK and MSK/RSK in SCCM inhibited the phenotypic change into floating suspension. Furthermore, cells developed a neuronal-like appearance showing bipolar or multipolar cells with axonal processes after combined inhibition of ERK and MSK/RSK regardless of RB1 status (Figure 6—figure supplement 5a), which was coupled with suppression of EGFR (Figure 6—figure supplement 5b).
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5b.

claims.claim: The triple-mutant cells showed no induction of NETFs over 3 or 7 days of culture with different combinations of inhibitors, both in normal media and SCCM.
claims.source: However, the triple-mutant cells, including the neuronal-like cells, showed no induction of NETFs over 3 (Figure 6—figure supplement 5b) or 7 (Figure 6—figure supplement 5c) days of culture with different combinations of inhibitors, both in normal media and SCCM.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5b and c.

claims.claim: This mechanism was not applicable across all cell lines assessed, indicative of the multifactorial mechanisms by which ERK suppresses NE differentiation in a context-dependent manner.
claims.source: However, it should be noted that this mechanism was not applicable across all cell lines we assessed, indicative of the multifactorial mechanisms by which ERK suppresses NE differentiation in a context-dependent manner.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the differential responses of different cell lines to CBP/p300 inhibition.

claims.claim: H2107 and H524 harbor mutations in EP300 while H82 is EP300 wild-type.
claims.source: Indeed, H2107 and H524 harbor mutations in EP300 while H82 is EP300 wild-type (Figure 7b), which might contribute to relatively low NE differentiation in H82 (Figure 1g) and its increased permissiveness to ERK-induced CBP/p300 HAT activity and NE factor suppression.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: EP300 mutation status might contribute to relatively low NE differentiation in H82 and its increased permissiveness to ERK-induced CBP/p300 HAT activity and NE factor suppression.
claims.source: Indeed, H2107 and H524 harbor mutations in EP300 while H82 is EP300 wild-type (Figure 7b), which might contribute to relatively low NE differentiation in H82 (Figure 1g) and its increased permissiveness to ERK-induced CBP/p300 HAT activity and NE factor suppression.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the EP300 mutation status and differential responses to CBP/p300 inhibition.

claims.claim: H2107 expresses MYCL while H82 and H524 are MYC high.
claims.source: As H2107 expresses MYCL while H82 and H524 are MYC high (Figure 7b), this could also underlie the differential response to ERK induction, such as those seen on cell growth and the involvement of CBP/p300 activation and H3K27ac in mediating NETF suppression.
claims.evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 7b.

claims.claim: MYC status could underlie the differential response to ERK induction in SCLC cell lines.
claims.source: As H2107 expresses MYCL while H82 and H524 are MYC high (Figure 7b), this could also underlie the differential response to ERK induction, such as those seen on cell growth and the involvement of CBP/p300 activation and H3K27ac in mediating NETF suppression.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the MYC status and differential responses observed.

claims.claim: ERK2 kinase activity plays a central role in inhibition of NE differentiation in all SCLC cell lines assessed.
claims.source: Nevertheless, our work clearly demonstrated that ERK2 kinase activity plays a central role in inhibition of NE differentiation in all SCLC cell lines assessed.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by ERK2 knockdown and inhibitor experiments across all cell lines.

claims.claim: ERK2 is known to directly shift transcriptional machinery in a kinase-dependent manner.
claims.source: As ERK2 is known to directly shift transcriptional machinery in a kinase-dependent manner (Hamilton et al., 2019; Göke et al., 2013), direct enhancer regulation by ERK2 may be involved in our model, with ERK-mediated chromatin remodeling independent of CBP/p300 activity also playing an important role in specific contexts (Figure 7c).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Hamilton et al., 2019 and Göke et al., 2013.

claims.claim: Direct enhancer regulation by ERK2 may be involved in NE suppression, with ERK-mediated chromatin remodeling independent of CBP/p300 activity also playing an important role in specific contexts.
claims.source: As ERK2 is known to directly shift transcriptional machinery in a kinase-dependent manner (Hamilton et al., 2019; Göke et al., 2013), direct enhancer regulation by ERK2 may be involved in our model, with ERK-mediated chromatin remodeling independent of CBP/p300 activity also playing an important role in specific contexts (Figure 7c).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the known functions of ERK2 and the cell line-specific responses observed.

claims.claim: Mutant-KRAS induction in SCLC more robustly suppresses NE differentiation and affects growth morphology than mutant-EGFR induction.
claims.source: We showed that mutant-KRAS induction in SCLC more robustly suppresses NE differentiation and affects growth morphology than mutant-EGFR induction.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing the effects of KRASG12V and EGFRL858R induction.

claims.claim: The differential effects of KRASG12V versus EGFRL858R are explained by the different potency of ERK activation between these two LUAD oncoproteins.
claims.source: The former is explained by the different potency of ERK activation between these two LUAD oncoproteins and is in line with the fact that KRAS mutations are not detected in SCLC specimens (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the differential ERK activation levels and is consistent with genomic data.

claims.claim: Loss of ERK2 and negative ERK2 expression are specific features of the neuroendocrine carcinoma component of gastric mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma.
claims.source: Moreover, a recent study highlighted the potentially deleterious effect of activated ERK in NE tumors by demonstrating that loss of ERK2 and negative ERK2 expression are specific features of the neuroendocrine carcinoma component of gastric mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma (Sun et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Sun et al., 2020.

claims.claim: FGFR amplification is observed in 6% of SCLC cases.
claims.source: Although one major exception for this scenario is FGFR amplification that is observed in 6% of SCLC cases (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015) and is anticipated to activate the MAPK pathway, another recent study showed that FGFR1 is disadvantageous for the development of typical central SCLC with NE differentiation using a Rb1flox/flox;Trp53flox/flox;LSL-Fgfr1K656E mouse model (Ferone et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by citations to Peifer et al., 2012 and George et al., 2015.

claims.claim: FGFR1 is disadvantageous for the development of typical central SCLC with NE differentiation.
claims.source: Although one major exception for this scenario is FGFR amplification that is observed in 6% of SCLC cases (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015) and is anticipated to activate the MAPK pathway, another recent study showed that FGFR1 is disadvantageous for the development of typical central SCLC with NE differentiation using a Rb1flox/flox;Trp53flox/flox;LSL-Fgfr1K656E mouse model (Ferone et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ferone et al., 2020.

claims.claim: A global or local increase in H3K27ac is incompatible with SCLC.
claims.source: The recurrently observed inactivating gene alterations of CREBBP/EP300 (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015; Rudin et al., 2012) in SCLC, as well as in EGFR-mutant LUAD tumors that subsequently undergo TKI-induced SCLC transformation (Offin et al., 2019), suggest that a global or local increase in H3K27ac is incompatible with SCLC.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the recurrent inactivating mutations in CBP/p300 in SCLC.

claims.claim: HDAC inhibitor treatment strongly suppressed NETFs in SCLC cells.
claims.source: Indeed, HDAC inhibitor treatment, which was shown to inhibit SCLC growth (Jia et al., 2018), strongly suppressed NETFs in SCLC cells (Figure 4d), despite potential specificity issues related to these inhibitors.
claims.evidence: This is demonstrated by western blot data shown in Figure 4d.

claims.claim: The use of HDAC inhibitors during treatment with EGFR-TKIs might be an option to prevent SCLC transformation in EGFR-mutant LUAD at a high risk of SCLC transformation.
claims.source: Nevertheless, our results imply that the use of HDAC inhibitors during treatment with EGFR-TKIs might be an option to prevent SCLC transformation in EGFR-mutant LUAD at a high risk of SCLC transformation.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation that HDAC inhibition suppresses NE factors.

claims.claim: SCLC transformation from LUAD requires specific conditions in the background of p53/RB loss, including lack of both second site EGFR mutations and bypass pathway mutations that reactivate MAPK signaling and ETS TFs, and alterations in epigenetic modifiers such as CBP/p300.
claims.source: We propose that SCLC transformation from LUAD requires specific conditions in the background of p53/RB loss, including lack of both second site EGFR mutations and bypass pathway mutations that reactivate MAPK signaling and ETS TFs, and alterations in epigenetic modifiers such as CBP/p300 to reduce H3K27ac levels and alter chromatin accessibility, rendering gene expression suitable for NE differentiation.
claims.evidence: This is a proposed model based on the study's findings and observations from resistant cells.

results.result: SCLC is characterized by neuroendocrine differentiation, frequent TP53/RB1 inactivation, absence of EGFR expression, low MAPK activity, and rare EGFR/KRAS mutations, contrasting with LUAD where EGFR/KRAS mutations are highly prevalent.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C24 establish the baseline molecular characteristics of SCLC versus LUAD through citations to established literature (Gazdar et al., 2017; Travis et al., 2015; Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015; Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network, 2014) and data presented in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b. These are well-established facts in the field supported by multiple independent studies.

results.result: Western blot analysis of lung cancer cell lines demonstrates an inverse association between EGFR expression and neuroendocrine differentiation, with SCLC cell lines completely lacking EGFR while expressing NE markers, and KRAS mutations never identified in SCLC genomic data.
results.evaluation: Claims C25-C29 are directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a (western blots) and Figure 1—figure supplement 1b (genomic analysis). The western blot clearly shows absence of EGFR in SCLC lines and presence of NE markers, while genomic data from cBioPortal confirms absence of KRAS mutations in SCLC.

results.result: Conditional expression of KRASG12V or EGFRL858R in SCLC cell lines induces phenotypic transition from suspended to adherent growth and suppresses neuroendocrine transcription factors, with KRASG12V showing more potent effects than EGFRL858R, correlating with stronger ERK1/2 phosphorylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C30-C35 are well-supported by multiple experimental approaches shown in Figure 1c-h: microscopy images demonstrate morphological changes, crystal violet assays quantify adherent cells, western blots show NE marker suppression and differential ERK phosphorylation, and GSEA demonstrates shift from high to low NE differentiation. The data consistently show KRASG12V has stronger effects than EGFRL858R across all assays.

results.result: MYC protein and MYC target genes are downregulated after KRASG12V induction, and YAP1 upregulation is only observed in H82 cells, suggesting the NE suppression is not driven by a MYC-YAP1 axis.
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C39 are supported by western blot data (Figure 1f), GSEA analysis (Figure 1—figure supplement 2f), and microarray data showing YAP1 upregulation only in H82 cells. The conclusion that MYC-YAP1 axis is not responsible is logically inferred from the observation that YAP1 is only upregulated in one of three cell lines despite all showing NE suppression.

results.result: Single-cell-derived clones show heterogeneous response to KRASG12V induction with mixed adherent and suspended populations, where adherent cells lose NE factors more than suspended cells, and isolated suspended cells do not give rise to adherent cells with attenuated KRASG12V expression over time.
results.evaluation: Claims C40-C43 are supported by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a-b showing clonal analysis and western blots of separated cell populations. The data demonstrate heterogeneity in response and differential NE factor loss between adherent and suspended populations, supporting the conclusion of heterogeneous effects.

results.result: ERK inhibitor SCH772984 rescues suppression of neuroendocrine transcription factors after KRASG12V induction, and siRNA knockdown experiments demonstrate ERK2, but not ERK1, is the dominant mediator of NE factor suppression.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C46 are directly supported by western blot data in Figure 2a (ERK inhibitor rescue) and Figure 2b (siRNA knockdown). The data clearly show restoration of NE factors with ERK inhibition and ERK2 knockdown but not ERK1 knockdown, providing strong evidence for ERK2 as the dominant node.

results.result: AKT inhibition with MK-2206 does not prevent suppression of neuroendocrine transcription factors after KRASG12V induction, indicating the PI3K/AKT pathway is not responsible for NE dedifferentiation.
results.evaluation: Claim C47 is supported by western blot data in Figure 2c showing that despite complete suppression of phospho-AKT, NE factors remain suppressed upon doxycycline treatment. This provides clear evidence that AKT is not required for NE suppression.

results.result: Combined inhibition of ERK and AKT reverses the suspended-to-adherent phenotypic transition in H82 and H524 cells, while ERK2 is the central hub for suppression of neuroendocrine regulators, indicating both pathways are required for growth phenotype changes but only ERK2 for NE suppression.
results.evaluation: Claims C48-C50 are supported by crystal violet staining and viability assays in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-b showing that combined ERK/AKT inhibition reverses phenotypic changes. The conclusion that both are required for phenotype but ERK2 is central for NE suppression is logically inferred from comparing the differential effects of single versus combined inhibition.

results.result: HES1 is strongly induced by mutant EGFR/KRAS in an ERK-dependent but NOTCH-independent manner in SCLC cells, but HES1 knockout does not restore NE factors, indicating HES1 is not responsible for ERK-mediated NE suppression.
results.evaluation: Claims C51-C56 are supported by microarray data, western blots (Figure 2—figure supplement 4c-d), NOTCH inhibitor experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 4e), and HES1 knockout experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 4f). The data consistently show HES1 induction is ERK-dependent but NOTCH-independent, and that HES1 elimination does not rescue NE factors.

results.result: REST and SOX9 are upregulated by KRASG12V in an ERK-dependent manner, but siRNA knockdown of REST and CRISPR knockout of SOX9 do not restore ERK-mediated suppression of neuroendocrine factors, indicating these transcription factors are not responsible for lineage transformation.
results.evaluation: Claims C57-C61 are supported by microarray data, RT-qPCR (Figure 2—figure supplement 5b-c), western blots (Figure 2—figure supplement 5d-e), and knockout experiments (Figure 2—figure supplement 5c,f). The data show upregulation of REST and SOX9 but lack of rescue upon their elimination, supporting the conclusion they are not responsible for NE suppression.

results.result: Mutant EGFR and KRAS alter global histone marks in SCLC cells, dramatically increasing H3K9ac, H3K14ac, and H3K27ac in H82 and H524 cells while decreasing H3K4me3 in H2107 cells, suggesting ERK-mediated NE suppression depends on altered chromatin structures that vary by SCLC subtype.
results.evaluation: Claims C62-C65 are directly supported by western blot data in Figure 3 showing differential changes in histone marks across cell lines. The inference that chromatin structure changes vary by subtype is reasonable given the differential patterns observed between ASCL1-high (H2107) and NEUROD1-high (H82, H524) cell lines.

results.result: Over 90% of H3K27ac depends on CBP/p300 histone acetyltransferases, which are recurrently inactivated in SCLC and enriched in EGFR-mutant LUAD undergoing SCLC transformation, while ERK directly and indirectly activates CBP/p300, suggesting SCLC evolves to maintain low H3K27ac and that ERK-mediated CBP/p300 activation may drive lineage transformation.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C72 are supported by multiple citations (Jin et al., 2011; Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015; Rudin et al., 2012; Offin et al., 2019; Ait-Si-Ali et al., 1999; Liu et al., 2016; Soloaga et al., 2003; Josefowicz et al., 2016) and illustrated in Figure 4a. The inference about SCLC evolution and lineage transformation is reasonable based on the convergent evidence from mutations and pathway activation.

results.result: MSK inhibition modestly prevents suppression of BRN2 and NEUROD1 but not INSM1, while CBP/p300 inhibitor A-485 at 400 nM restores INSM1, BRN2, and NEUROD1 expression and reduces H3K27ac in H82 cells without affecting H3K9ac and H3K14ac.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C75 are directly supported by western blot data in Figure 4b-c and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a. The data clearly show differential rescue effects of MSK versus CBP/p300 inhibition and specificity of A-485 for H3K27ac.

results.result: HDAC inhibitor trichostatin A eliminates neuroendocrine factor expression even without KRASG12V induction, suggesting H3K27ac levels must be restricted to maintain SCLC lineage.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C77 are supported by western blot data in Figure 4d showing elimination of NE factors with HDAC inhibition. The inference that H3K27ac must be restricted is logical given that increasing acetylation (via HDAC inhibition) eliminates NE factors.

results.result: Constitutively activated ERK suppresses neuroendocrine transcription factors partly through MSK but mostly via chromatin reconfiguration by CBP/p300 in H82 cells, though this mechanism does not apply to H2107 and H524 cells.
results.evaluation: Claim C78 is supported by the combined data from Figure 4—figure supplement 1a showing that A-485 treatment rescues NE factors only in H82 cells but not in H2107 and H524 cells. The cell line-specific response is clearly demonstrated, supporting the conclusion of context-dependent mechanisms.

results.result: ATAC-seq analysis shows KRASG12V induction causes overall increase in chromatin accessibility while ERK inhibitor SCH772984 reduces accessible chromatin, with altered accessibility primarily in intergenic and intronic regions consistent with regulatory region changes.
results.evaluation: Claims C79-C81 are directly supported by ATAC-seq data presented in the text and Figure 5a-b and Figure 5—figure supplement 1c-d. The quantification of peaks gained/lost and genomic distribution analysis provide clear evidence for the stated conclusions.

results.result: Motif analysis of ATAC-seq data reveals doxycycline treatment increases accessibility at ETV1, ETV4, and AP-1 motifs while reducing accessibility at NEUROD1 and ASCL1 motifs, with ERK inhibitor SCH772984 reversing this pattern.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C84 are directly supported by motif analysis data shown in Figure 5c-d. The data clearly demonstrate the stated changes in motif accessibility and reversal with ERK inhibition.

results.result: Peaks gained upon doxycycline induction are significantly associated with H3K27ac-decorated chromatin regions in normal human lung (p=0.002), with markedly increased accessibility at ETV1/ETV4 motifs in H524 and H82 cells and reduced accessibility at ASCL1/NEUROD1 motifs in H524 and H2107 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C87 are supported by permutation testing (Figure 5e-f, p=0.002) and motif occupancy profiles (Figure 5g-h). The statistical significance and clear visualization of differential accessibility provide strong support for these conclusions.

results.result: ATAC-seq demonstrates global chromatin rewiring at ETS transcriptional targets upon KRASG12V induction, and ETS transcription factors (ETV1, ETV4, ETV5) are upregulated at mRNA level by MAPK activation, suggesting an ETS-mediated program may suppress neuroendocrine differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C88-C90 are supported by ATAC-seq data showing changes at ETS motifs and microarray data (Supplementary file 1 and Figure 6a) showing ETS TF upregulation. The inference about ETS-mediated NE suppression is reasonable given the convergent chromatin accessibility and expression data.

results.result: Microarray data shows inverse relationship between PEA3 family ETS transcription factors and neuroendocrine transcription factors across SCLC and LUAD cell lines, and mutant KRAS upregulates ETV4 in H82/H524 and ETV5 in all three SCLC lines, which is completely reversed by ERK inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C91-C93 are supported by microarray data (Figure 6b) and western blot data (Figure 6c). The heat map clearly shows inverse expression patterns, and western blots demonstrate ERK-dependent upregulation of ETV4 and ETV5.

results.result: Conditional expression of ETV1 or ETV5 in SCLC cells suppresses specific neuroendocrine transcription factors in a cell line-dependent manner and unexpectedly transforms cells to an adherent phenotype, most strongly in H82 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C94-C96 are supported by western blot data (Figure 6d-e) showing NE factor suppression and microscopy images (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) showing morphological changes. The data demonstrate both molecular and phenotypic effects of ETS overexpression.

results.result: siRNA knockdown of ETV4 modestly restores INSM1 while ETV5 knockdown restores NEUROD1, and dual knockdown jointly increases INSM1 and CD56, suggesting functional redundancy among ETS factors in suppressing neuroendocrine differentiation.
results.evaluation: Claims C97-C99 are supported by western blot data in Figure 6f showing differential and additive effects of single and dual knockdowns. The inference of functional redundancy is reasonable given the additive effects observed with dual knockdown.

results.result: Nuclear CIC is expressed in SCLC cells and downregulated after KRASG12V induction in an ERK-dependent manner, and CIC knockdown suppresses neuroendocrine factors but does not induce ETS factors, while CIC overexpression does not prevent NE suppression, suggesting ERK-mediated ETS upregulation does not occur via CIC inhibition.
results.evaluation: Claims C100-C104 are supported by western blot data from fractionated lysates (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a), siRNA knockdown (Figure 6—figure supplement 2b), and overexpression experiments (Figure 6—figure supplement 2c). The data consistently show CIC is not the mediator of ETS upregulation despite being regulated by ERK.

results.result: CBP/p300 inhibitor A-485 downregulates ERK-induced ETV4 and ETV5 in H82 cells but not in H2107 and H524 cells, indicating induction of PEA3 family ETS transcription factors is mediated by CBP/p300 HAT activity in H82 cells but not in H2107 and H524 cells.
results.evaluation: Claims C105, C110, C111 are supported by western blot data in Figure 6g and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a showing cell line-specific effects of A-485 on ETS factors. The differential response provides clear evidence for distinct mechanisms across cell lines.

results.result: ERG is induced by KRASG12V in H82 and H524 cells, and ERG inhibition provides modest restoration of neuroendocrine factors synergizing with MSK/RSK inhibition, while combined MSK/RSK and ERG inhibition rescues MYC but not key neuroendocrine transcription factors, suggesting ERK modulates transcription factors through multiple regulatory mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C106-C109 are supported by western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 3a-b showing ERG induction, effects of ERG inhibition, and differential rescue of MYC versus NE factors. The inference of multiple regulatory mechanisms is reasonable given the differential rescue patterns.

results.result: Dual p53/RB inactivation is ubiquitous in SCLC, and EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinomas with p53/RB loss are more likely to undergo SCLC transformation after tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C113 are supported by multiple citations (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015; Offin et al., 2019; Niederst et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017). These are well-established observations in the field.

results.result: In RB1-knockout PC9 and H1975 cells, SOX2 deregulation and neuroendocrine factor induction were not observed following osimertinib treatment, suggesting the lung adenocarcinoma lineage is more strictly maintained than AR-dependent prostate cancer in the context of dual p53/RB inactivation.
results.evaluation: Claims C114-C116 are supported by western blot data in Figure 6—figure supplement 4b showing lack of SOX2 deregulation and NE factor induction. The comparison to prostate cancer is supported by citation to Niederst et al., 2015, and the inference about lineage maintenance is reasonable.

results.result: In osimertinib-resistant clones, phospho-ERK remains detectable and neuroendocrine factors are not induced, with recurrent CIC mutations identified in H1975 resistant clones and prominent ETV5 upregulation in clones with CIC alterations, suggesting resistance mechanisms reactivating the ERK/CIC/ETS axis suppress neuroendocrine differentiation even with p53/RB loss.
results.evaluation: Claims C117-C121 are supported by western blot data (Figure 6—figure supplement 4f-g) and MSK-IMPACT sequencing (Figure 6—figure supplement 4e) showing persistent pERK, lack of NE factors, CIC mutations, and ETV5 upregulation. The inference about ERK/CIC/ETS axis suppressing NE differentiation is reasonable given the convergent molecular data.

results.result: Combined ERK and MSK/RSK inhibition in stem cell culture media induces neuronal-like morphology with axonal processes and suppresses EGFR in H1975 cells, but triple-mutant cells show no induction of neuroendocrine transcription factors over 3 or 7 days with various inhibitor combinations.
results.evaluation: Claims C122-C124 are supported by microscopy images (Figure 6—figure supplement 5a) and western blot data (Figure 6—figure supplement 5b-c). The data clearly show morphological changes and EGFR suppression but lack of NE factor induction despite neuronal-like appearance.

results.result: The ERK-CBP/p300 mechanism is not applicable across all SCLC cell lines assessed, with H2107 and H524 harboring EP300 mutations while H82 is wild-type, and differential MYC family expression (MYCL in H2107 vs MYC-high in H82/H524), suggesting these factors contribute to differential responses to ERK induction.
results.evaluation: Claims C125-C129 are supported by the differential responses observed across experiments and mutation/expression data shown in Figure 7b. The inference that EP300 status and MYC family expression contribute to differential responses is reasonable given the cell line-specific patterns, though causality is not definitively established.

results.result: ERK2 kinase activity plays a central role in inhibition of neuroendocrine differentiation in all SCLC cell lines assessed, and ERK2 is known to directly shift transcriptional machinery in a kinase-dependent manner, suggesting direct enhancer regulation by ERK2 and ERK-mediated chromatin remodeling independent of CBP/p300 may be involved.
results.evaluation: Claims C130-C132 are supported by ERK2 knockdown and inhibitor experiments across all cell lines (Figure 2b) and citations to Hamilton et al., 2019 and Göke et al., 2013. The inference about direct enhancer regulation is reasonable given the known functions of ERK2 and cell line-specific responses, though speculative.

results.result: Mutant KRAS induction more robustly suppresses neuroendocrine differentiation and affects growth morphology than mutant EGFR, explained by differential ERK activation potency, consistent with the absence of KRAS mutations in SCLC specimens.
results.evaluation: Claims C133-C134 are supported by comparing effects of KRASG12V versus EGFRL858R across multiple assays (Figures 1c-h) showing differential ERK phosphorylation and effects. The consistency with genomic data (Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015) strengthens the conclusion.

results.result: Loss of ERK2 and negative ERK2 expression are specific features of neuroendocrine carcinoma in gastric mixed adenoneuroendocrine carcinoma, and while FGFR amplification occurs in 6% of SCLC cases, FGFR1 is disadvantageous for typical central SCLC with neuroendocrine differentiation in mouse models.
results.evaluation: Claims C135-C137 are supported by citations to Sun et al., 2020; Peifer et al., 2012; George et al., 2015; and Ferone et al., 2020. These provide independent validation of the inverse relationship between MAPK/ERK activity and NE differentiation in other tumor types and model systems.

results.result: Recurrent inactivating mutations in CREBBP/EP300 in SCLC and transforming LUAD suggest increased H3K27ac is incompatible with SCLC, and HDAC inhibitor treatment strongly suppresses neuroendocrine transcription factors, implying HDAC inhibitors during EGFR-TKI treatment might prevent SCLC transformation.
results.evaluation: Claims C138-C139 are supported by citations and western blot data (Figure 4d). However, claim C140 is speculative inference without direct experimental validation. The authors acknowledge they could not demonstrate CBP/p300 inhibition promotes SCLC transformation, and the HDAC inhibitor suggestion is based on inverse reasoning that may not hold clinically. Additional validation would be needed.

results.result: SCLC transformation from lung adenocarcinoma requires specific conditions including p53/RB loss, lack of EGFR mutations and bypass pathway mutations reactivating MAPK/ETS, and alterations in epigenetic modifiers like CBP/p300 to reduce H3K27ac and alter chromatin accessibility.
results.evaluation: Claim C141 is a proposed model based on the study's findings but is explicitly speculative ("We propose"). While supported by observations from resistant cells showing MAPK reactivation prevents NE transformation, the authors acknowledge they could not force SCLC transformation experimentally. The model is reasonable but requires validation in appropriate model systems.
